note: An unusual profile: he clears the fitness-related criteria comfortably and fails the two that describe the customer's relationship to their own health. He is emphatically not deconditioned — a professional dancer, active his whole life, training four times a week, hypermobile rather than stiff — and he is a clean good-to-great case, wanting to add strength and load progression to an already strong movement base. Income is recorded as a match on the available evidence: he showed no price resistance whatsoever, asked the cost as a neutral data point, and was combining work and holiday in Dubai from a base in Belgium; nothing suggests constraint, though no financial detail was disclosed. He misses 'successful' in the sense the ICP means it — a dancer and movement teacher is not a business owner, physician or equivalent, and the rep never asked about work, so nothing establishes it. He misses 'neglected_health' outright and interestingly: health is not his neglected area, it is his profession. 'I'm pretty content with my body performance in my field.' That inversion is the finding — the offer's entire value proposition assumes a successful person who has let their health slide, and this prospect was the reverse, which is why two of the three pillars were rejected before they were finished.
